en: Vimānavatthu:
Purisavimāna,
Mahārathavagga
8. The First Mansion Story of the Needle “High is this mansion with its jeweled pillars,
extending twelve yojanas on all sides.”
Seven hundred lofty gabled chambers,
beautiful with pillars of beryl and adorned with golden ornaments;
there you eat, drink, and enjoy yourself.
And divine lutes play their lovely melodies; here,
divine flavors and the five strands of sensual pleasure abound,
while women adorned in gold dance.
“By what means do you have such a complexion...
[and so on] ...and your complexion illuminates all directions?”
Thus the young god was delighted...
[as before] ...the fruit of which action this is.
“That which one gives does not remain;
rather, that which one should give is better.
A needle given is better than the needle itself.”
"Because of that, my complexion is such as this...
and my complexion shines forth in all directions."
The first Sūcivimāna is the eighth.
